sources.title: Report of the Secretary-General on the activities of the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa (S/2025/772)
sources.organization: United Nations Secretary-General / United Nations Office for Central Africa
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional climate conditions in June–August 2025 and a reported Namibe incident on 17 August 2025.
sources.methodology: UN Secretary-General's regional political and humanitarian reporting, including climate-service information.
sources.limitations: The report gives no independent causal assessment or names for the communities involved.

sources.title: Nationally Determined Contribution of Angola 2025 (NDC 3.0)
sources.organization: Republic of Angola, Ministry of Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate assessments and adaptation priorities, with historical examples and plans through 2035.
sources.methodology: NDC reviews national climate and sector plans.
sources.limitations: Commitments are not independently evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Eastern and Southern Africa Region Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2, 1 January–31 December 2024
sources.organization: UNICEF Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional and Angola situation and response reporting for calendar year 2024, with some cited water-point data from 2022.
sources.methodology: Regional UNICEF situation report aggregates country-office needs and response reporting.
sources.limitations: Some water-point estimates are dated; the report gives limited local disaggregation.

sources.title: Angola Preparedness for Resilient Recovery Project: First Project Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Project progress and disaster-preparedness activities reported for September 2014–September 2015.
sources.methodology: UNDP project progress report records preparedness, training and recovery-assessment activities.
sources.limitations: It is a first-year report; many subsequent provincial and municipal plans were targets, not verified results.

sources.title: Angola Food Security Outlook, June 2026–January 2027: Likely El Niño-induced dryness to lead to outcomes aligned with Crisis in southern areas by November
sources.temporal_coverage: Current food-security conditions through June 2026 and outlook through January 2027.
sources.methodology: FEWS NET synthesizes weather, crop, market, livelihood and nutrition evidence.
sources.limitations: Not a census; some nutrition surveillance is not representative.

claims.paraphrase: UNOCA reports 17 August clashes between two unnamed communities in Namibe over dam access amid prolonged drought; 12–20 people were killed and thousands displaced.
institutions: United Nations Office for Central Africa
Climate Application and Forecasting Centre of Central Africa
claims.limitations: The report supplies a fatality range and does not independently test the stated relationship.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report places the clash over dam access amid prolonged drought.

claims.paraphrase: NDC links drainage and erosion deficits to flood and life risks in urban Luanda.
NDC identifies low-income people, Indigenous communities, small producers and rural women as especially vulnerable.
Drought may draw girls into distant water collection, increasing early-marriage and gender-based-violence risks.
claims.limitations: Risks are described, not measured or located.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Distant water collection under drought increases girls' exposure to gender-based violence and early marriage.

claims.paraphrase: NDC reports over one million people affected in Huíla, Namibe and Cunene during 2015–16 drought, with $286m damage and about $437m losses.
claims.limitations: NDC cites prior assessments; method unclear.

claims.paraphrase: NDC notes watershed and reservoir data gaps and insufficient technical capacity for long-term water projections.
claims.limitations: Coverage and service effects are unquantified.

claims.locator: PDF printed pp. 53–54, ecosystem and water-resources sections
claims.paraphrase: These wetlands and peatlands support rural water and livelihoods but face fire and land-use pressure.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 3, Angola situation overview
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF attributes drought affecting 5.6 million people to El Niño-era rainfall deficits; it reports 1.2 million water-scarce people and 50–80% of southern water points non-operational in 2022.
claims.limitations: The national drought estimate and older regional water-point estimate have different periods and denominators.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 3, Angola situation overview
claims.paraphrase: The report links crop losses to delayed, below-average rain and says inflation, currency weakness and fuel-subsidy removal further worsened food insecurity.
claims.limitations: The report identifies several concurrent pressures and does not isolate their relative effects.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 3, Angola health response
claims.paraphrase: In drought-affected Huíla and Cunene, UNICEF reports measles vaccination for 11,587 at-risk children and maternal or child health services for 251,559 women and children.
claims.limitations: Reported service reach is not an evaluation of health outcomes attributable to drought response.

claims.paraphrase: In August 2015, Angola's Civil Protection Commission and UNDP trained 43 national and provincial officials in Luanda on needs assessment and resilient recovery.
claims.limitations: The report records one training activity; it does not evaluate later capacity or plans.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 3, flood-recovery field exercise
claims.paraphrase: After Benguela floods, a CNPC–UNDP exercise assessed recovery needs in Lobito, Catumbela and Cabrais, including housing, health, education, livelihoods and agriculture.
claims.limitations: The report describes a pilot assessment and planned recovery plan, not completed recovery outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: The report cites OCHA estimates that 2013–14 drought affected 1.8 million people in Cunene, Namibe, parts of Benguela and Huíla; about 700,000 faced food-insecurity risk.
affected_groups: people at risk of food insecurity
claims.limitations: This UNDP report relays OCHA estimates; the underlying assessment was not separately inspected.

claims.paraphrase: 2025/26 rains were delayed and dry, with below-average harvests and crop failures at Oncócua, Cunene.
claims.limitations: Other areas are broad regional aggregates.

claims.paraphrase: Projected dryness may delay southern water recharge and pasture, prompting earlier movement toward Namibia and reducing veterinary access.
claims.scenario: FEWS NET's most-likely outlook assumes El Niño and below-average October 2026–January 2027 rainfall.
claims.limitations: June 2026 forecast, not an October conditions update.

claims.locator: Angola outlook, key messages and projected outcomes through January 2027
claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET projects 1.0–1.49 million people needing assistance in southern agropastoral areas in November 2026–January 2027, with IPC Phase 3-aligned outcomes.
claims.scenario: FEWS NET's most-likely outlook through January 2027.
claims.limitations: June 2026 estimate, not an October conditions update.

claims.locator: Angola outlook, current outcomes as of June 2026
claims.paraphrase: Some isolated herders in Cunene, Namibe and Cuando Cubango with prior-drought herd losses and few alternatives are assessed as likely IPC Phase 3.
claims.limitations: June assessment, not an October update or all households in these provinces.

search_audit.outcome: No opened country-specific source linked insecurity to impaired climate adaptation or disaster services. The historical civil-war legacy in FEWS NET concerns urbanization, not adaptation disruption.

search_audit.outcome: NDC water-monitoring gaps, 2015 CNPC–UNDP training and recovery planning, UNICEF health response and FEWS NET livelihood conditions were verified in full text; historic project outputs are not presented as current capacity.

gaps: No pre-existing AGO country dossier was present under countries/ in this worktree; this is a new-country Phase 2 extraction.
The UN Secretary-General report explicitly relates the Namibe clash to dam access amid prolonged drought, but it does not establish causality independently or identify the communities.
No opened source connected conflict or insecurity to weaker climate adaptation, climate-service delivery or disaster response; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

The World Bank risk report PDF exceeded the reader size limit, the UNDRR full profile was unavailable beyond landing-page metadata, and the 2026 OHRLLS PDF returned HTTP 403; snippets and metadata were not used for claims.
The NDC uses older southern-province groupings for some historic statistics despite Angola's 2025 administrative reorganization; those aggregate figures are not mapped to new province boundaries.
FEWS NET's outlook is based on information through 30 June 2026 and its projected food-security outcomes are not observed results.
